name: Ray-Box Intersection via Quad Rasterization
definition: A voxel rendering technique where each voxel is represented by a single point in a vertex array. The point is sized to cover the voxel's projected area, and the actual voxel geometry (cube) is intersected with a ray in the fragment shader using an optimized ray-box intersection test.
summary: Ray-Box Intersection via Quad Rasterization renders voxels as point primitives sized to cover their projected area, using fragment shader ray tracing to determine visibility and avoiding explicit cube face rasterization.
